title: Decide: exercises as files in db/exercises/ or rows in the database
description: CLAUDE.md and the /add-exercise skill assume exercises live as Markdown files in db/exercises/ and are loaded by db:seed. The alternative is rows in the database edited through an admin screen. Files are reviewable in git and easy for the owner to write; a database is needed once other people author exercises.
design: Files now does not close the door on a database later: the loader can become an importer. The coach-only material is the part that must stay out of any rendered query either way.
acceptance_criteria: - The choice is made and, if it differs from the files assumption, CLAUDE.md and the /add-exercise skill are updated
notes:
Blocks the exercise loader. Plan ref: open questions.

--- 2026-10-17 decided: files ---
Recorded in docs/decisions/0002-exercises-as-files.md.

Chose files in db/exercises/ (<slug>.md plus <slug>.coach.md), loaded by an
idempotent upsert in db/seeds.rb keyed on slug. Matches what CLAUDE.md and the
/add-exercise skill already assumed, so the acceptance criterion's 'if it differs
from the files assumption' branch does not apply -- no CLAUDE.md or skill edits
needed.

Deciding fact: for all of Phase 1 the only author is the owner, so an admin
screen buys nothing and costs an authoring UI, validation surfaces and an answer
to 'who may edit'. The structural argument mattered more than the convenience
one: coach-only material in a file that nothing loads cannot leak through a
careless select, whereas the same material in the database is one query away
from a user-facing page.

The loader is the seam for later: it becomes an importer when organizations need
database-backed authoring, which is also this bead's revisit trigger.
close_reason: Decided: files in db/exercises/, loaded by db/seeds.rb. Recorded in docs/decisions/0002-exercises-as-files.md. Matches the existing CLAUDE.md and /add-exercise assumption, so no doc updates were needed.

title: Data model: users, exercises, attempts
description: Migrations and models for users, exercises and attempts. users: unique github_id (logins can change, ids do not). exercises: slug, title, summary, body_md, difficulty, topic, minutes, published_at. attempts: user, exercise, outcome, minutes, plan, stuck_on, learned; append-only, so retrying an exercise adds a row.
design: Use database constraints, not just validations: unique github_id and slug, check constraints on difficulty (easy/medium/hard) and outcome (solved/partial/stuck), minutes between 0 and 600. Rails enums for difficulty and outcome. Foreign keys on, attempts cascade on user delete.
acceptance_criteria:
- Model tests cover every constraint and validation
- Each constraint also fails at the database level, not only in Rails
- Indexes exist on attempts (user_id, created_at) and attempts (user_id, exercise_id)
notes:
Plan ref 1.1. A good one to write yourself and review with /sparring. The schema was worked out in the earlier Workers/D1 prototype.

--- 2026-10-17 who-writes conflict, resolved to the live answer ---
This bead said 'A good one to write yourself and review with /sparring' and
carried the owner-writes label. Asked the CLAUDE.md 'offer once' question in
session on 2026-10-17 and the owner chose 'I write it, you review' instead.
Going with the live answer as the more recent instruction; label swapped to
claude-writes so the tracker stops contradicting the decision. Flagged to the
owner in-session in case they answered without this note in view.

--- 2026-10-17 implemented in 33c229b ---

Three migrations, three models, fixtures, 41 tests / 165 assertions. bin/ci green
in 5.41s; CI run 39076077693 green on main across all five jobs.

Acceptance criteria:
 [x] Model tests cover every constraint and validation -- presence, uniqueness,
     both enums, the 0..600 minutes range including its boundaries, integer-only
     minutes, the published scope and published? across all three publication
     states, and the append-only retry case.
 [x] Each constraint also fails at the database level. Every one has a paired
     test using insert_all!, which bypasses the model: check constraints raise
     StatementInvalid, unique raises RecordNotUnique, NOT NULL raises
     NotNullViolation, bad references raise InvalidForeignKey. Cascade and
     restrict are tested through delete rather than destroy so the database,
     not Active Record, is what refuses.
 [x] Indexes on attempts (user_id, created_at) and (user_id, exercise_id), with
     a test asserting both exist so a later migration cannot quietly drop them.

Decisions made while writing, flag any you disagree with:
 - github_id is bigint, not string. GitHub ids are numeric.
 - users has no name or avatar_url yet; deferred to codegym-ir5, where a page
   will actually consume them.
 - minutes range is inclusive 0..600 on both tables, matching the design note
   literally rather than inventing a lower bound of 1.
 - exercises.summary is NOT NULL, since every library card shows it.
 - Deleting an attempted exercise is refused outright (restrict), rather than
   cascading. The design specified cascade only for user deletes, and attempt
   history is the user's, not the content's.
 - t.references :user is index: false; the composite (user_id, created_at)
   index serves user_id-only lookups as its left prefix.

Two Rails-on-main gotchas, both now commented in the code:
 - enum needs a HASH for a string-backed column. A bare array makes Rails pair
   labels with each_with_index (enum.rb:263 on ba3572c), so difficulty would
   have stored '0' and tripped its own check constraint. Caught before commit by
   reading the source, then confirmed via difficulty_for_database.
 - insert_all passes on_duplicate: :skip, so it silently swallows unique
   violations; the constraint tests use insert_all! (on_duplicate: :raise). The
   first version of the user test passed for the wrong reason until this was
   found.
close_reason: Migrations, models, fixtures and 41 tests in 33c229b. Every constraint tested at both the model and database level; both required indexes present and asserted. bin/ci green, CI green on main.

Coach-only material goes in <slug>.coach.md and is never loaded here. If the storage question resolves differently, update CLAUDE.md and the skill.

- Every friction point is filed as its own bead

description: Pick the host and ship it. A single VPS with Kamal is the natural fit for SQLite and the Solid stack, and the repo already has a Dockerfile and .kamal/. Create the production GitHub OAuth app, set credentials, and write a short deploy runbook.

acceptance_criteria:
- A decision record names the host and why
- Production sign-in works end to end
- A runbook covers deploy, rollback and where logs are
notes: Plan ref 1.12. Write the decision record with /decision-record.

title: Attempt form: log how it went
description: Outcome, minutes (prefilled from the timer), plan, stuck-on and learned, with length caps. Saving redirects with a flash and shows the user's last five attempts on that exercise. Anyone not signed in is sent to sign in and returned here.
acceptance_criteria:
- Invalid outcome or minutes outside 0 to 600 is rejected with a clear message
- Text fields are capped (4000 characters) on both client and server
- A user cannot write or read another user's attempts

title: Library page with filters and solved/tried status
description: The home page lists published exercises. Filter by difficulty and topic inside a Turbo Frame, so filtering does not reload the page. Signed-in users see solved and tried-N-times status on each exercise; signed-out visitors see the library and a prompt to sign in.
acceptance_criteria:
- Filters work without a full page load and survive a refresh via the URL
- Status reflects the signed-in user's attempts only

title: Make GitHub CI match bin/ci, and keep Dependabot off the Rails pin
description: Rails generated .github/workflows/ci.yml and .github/dependabot.yml. Check that the workflow runs the same checks as bin/ci and passes on main. Also make sure Dependabot cannot propose Rails changes: ADR 0001 says Rails moves only through bin/bump-rails, one bump per commit.
acceptance_criteria:
- The CI workflow is green on main and runs the same steps as bin/ci
- Dependabot ignores the rails/rails git source (or is limited to other gems)
notes:
Plan ref 0.3.

--- 2026-10-17 progress (config done, verification blocked) ---

DONE: Dependabot fence. .github/dependabot.yml now ignores the 13 gems that
resolve from the rails/rails git remote, with a comment pointing at ADR 0001.
Enumerated explicitly rather than as active*/action* globs so it cannot silently
swallow an unrelated gem such as activerecord-session_store. Only 'rails' is
declared in the Gemfile, so that is the name Dependabot acts on; the rest are
belt-and-braces.

DONE: step parity, with two fixes.
  - Added a 'Replant seeds' step to the test job, mirroring 'Tests: Seeds' in
    config/ci.rb. The workflow had no equivalent, and the exercise loader runs
    through db:seed (codegym-lak), so a broken loader would have been caught
    locally but not in CI.
  - Brakeman flags now match config/ci.rb exactly. Note: --exit-on-warn and
    --exit-on-error are Brakeman 8.1 DEFAULTS (confirmed in --help, which marks
    both '(Default)'), so the generated job was not actually passing on warnings.
    This is parity plus pinning the behavior explicitly, not a bug fix.
  - Also stripped 2 pre-existing trailing-whitespace lines, per .editorconfig.

Accepted, non-bug differences: lint uses 'bin/rubocop -f github' (formatter only,
same checks and exit code); bin/ci's 'Setup' step has no workflow counterpart
because bundler-cache plus db:test:prepare cover it in CI.

OPEN FORK: system tests. The workflow has a system-test job; config/ci.rb has
'Tests: System' commented out. One of the two should move. Uncommenting it locally
makes the pre-commit gate need a browser and run slower; dropping the CI job loses
coverage that codegym-oiz will depend on. Owner's call, not made yet.

BLOCKED: the second acceptance criterion, 'The CI workflow is green on main',
cannot be verified. There is no git remote and no GitHub repo (git remote -v is
empty; gh reports 'no git remotes found'), so this workflow has never executed.
The YAML parses and every step's command is proven locally by bin/ci (green in
5.24s), but that is not the same as a green run on GitHub. Keep this open until a
remote exists.

--- 2026-10-17 remote exists; first CI run is RED ---

Remote pushed: git@github.com:meaganewaller/codegym.git, PUBLIC, default main.
Local and origin/main both at b3f389a, so GitHub ran the PRE-FIX workflow; the
dependabot.yml and ci.yml changes above are still uncommitted.

Run 39071089044 (push, b3f389a): FAILURE. lint, scan_ruby, scan_js passed.
test and system-test both failed with the same error:

  db/schema.rb doesn't exist yet. Run `bin/rails db:migrate` to create it.

ROOT CAUSE, and it is a THIRD bin/ci-vs-workflow divergence beyond the two fixed
above: the workflow runs 'bin/rails db:test:prepare test', which hard-requires
db/schema.rb. config/ci.rb never calls db:test:prepare -- it relies on bin/setup
having run db:prepare. So local bin/ci is green while GitHub is red on the same
commit. Verified: there is no db/migrate directory and no db/schema.rb; only
db/cable_schema.rb, cache_schema.rb, queue_schema.rb and seeds.rb are tracked.
db/schema.rb is not gitignored, so it is committable once it exists.

This is the ordinary fresh-Rails-app case: zero migrations means no schema.rb.
Rather than commit a placeholder schema at version 0 that codegym-g70 would
immediately overwrite, 'green on main' should wait for g70's first migration to
produce a real schema.rb. Dependency added.

ALSO CONFIRMED, the hazard was real and not theoretical: Dependabot ran within a
minute of the push, against the unfenced config, and opened PR #1
'chore(deps): bump rails from ba3572c to e9aab74' -- branch
dependabot/bundler/rails-e9aab74. This is exactly what ADR 0001 rule 1 forbids:
a Rails move that does not go through bin/bump-rails and writes no bump-log row.
It also proves Dependabot bumps a branch-tracking git source and names the
dependency 'rails', which is what the ignore list targets. PR #1 needs closing
and the fence needs committing.

--- 2026-10-17 fence verified in production, before/after ---

Committed d02d520 (dependabot fence) and 1fbdb0f (ci.yml parity), pushed to
origin/main.

The fence is confirmed by observation, not just by reading the config:
  BEFORE (b3f389a, unfenced): the Dependabot bundler run opened PR #1 bumping
  Rails ba3572c -> e9aab74 within a minute of the push.
  AFTER (1fbdb0f, fenced): the equivalent bundler run completed success and
  opened no PR at all. Dependabot also auto-closed PR #1 at 22:25:02, the moment
  the ignore rule landed, and deleted its dependabot/bundler/rails-e9aab74
  branch. A comment citing ADR 0001 rule 1 was left on the PR for the record.

Side note for a future bump: upstream main had moved to e9aab74 as of today.

CI on 1fbdb0f is still FAILURE, with exactly one cause and nothing new:
'schema.rb doesn't exist yet' in the test and system-test jobs. lint, scan_ruby
and scan_js pass. The new 'Replant seeds' step is never reached, because the test
job dies on db:test:prepare first. So this remains blocked on codegym-g70's first
migration, as recorded above -- no further CI config work is needed or useful
until that lands.

--- 2026-10-17 CLOSED: green on main ---
codegym-g70's first migration landed in 33c229b and produced db/schema.rb, which
is what db:test:prepare needed. CI run 39076077693 on 33c229b: SUCCESS across all
five jobs -- test, system-test, scan_ruby, scan_js, lint.

Both acceptance criteria met. Dependabot fence verified by before/after behavior
(PR #1 opened unfenced, no PR and an auto-close once fenced). The remaining
system-test divergence is spun out to its own decision bead rather than left
hiding in these notes.
close_reason: CI run 39076077693 green on main across all five jobs; Dependabot fenced off the rails/rails git source and verified by behavior. Seeds step and Brakeman flags now mirror config/ci.rb. The system-test divergence is spun out to codegym-d5u.1.

title: Phase 0: Foundation
description: Get the Rails-on-main app to a documented, CI-green baseline so feature work starts from something known. Exit: bin/ci is green on a clean checkout, the baseline SHA is recorded in ADR 0001, the config and README are in place, and GitHub CI runs the same checks as bin/ci.

title: GitHub sign-in with database-backed sessions
description: Sign in with GitHub and nothing else. Ask for no scopes beyond the public profile. Upsert the user on github_id and refresh login, name and avatar each time. Add sign-out and a safe next-redirect that allows only same-site relative paths.
design: Take the pieces of the Rails authentication generator worth keeping (Session model, Current, an Authentication concern), drop the password flow, and add omniauth-github with omniauth-rails_csrf_protection so the request phase is POST-only. Sessions live in the database so they can be revoked.
acceptance_criteria:
- Tests use OmniAuth test mode for success, denial and a tampered state
- A forged, expired or revoked session is rejected
- A next parameter pointing off-site or starting with // is ignored
notes: Plan ref 1.4. A good one to write yourself and review with /sparring.

title: Boot the app, get bin/ci green, confirm the baseline
description: The app was generated on Rails main and the baseline SHA is recorded in ADR 0001. Confirm that bin/setup, bin/rails server and bin/ci all pass on a clean checkout, and that the SHA in the bump log matches the revision in Gemfile.lock.

- The bump log baseline row matches the rails/rails revision in Gemfile.lock

Plan ref 0.1. Verified 2026-10-17 on ruby 3.4.10, Rails 8.2.0.alpha.

title: Exercise page: Markdown rendering and the timer
description: Show one exercise: rendered Markdown, then a sticky timer that moves through plan, build and reflect phases (roughly the first sixth, the middle two thirds, and the last sixth of the time). The timer survives a reload and can be paused and reset.
design: Stimulus controller keyed by exercise slug, state in localStorage (guarded with try/catch), elapsed time derived from a start timestamp rather than counted by interval ticks, so a backgrounded tab does not drift. Exercise bodies are trusted content for now; sanitization becomes mandatory in the Teams phase.
acceptance_criteria:
- Choose and document the Markdown renderer and how its output is sanitized
- Reloading the page keeps the timer running
- Screen readers are told about phase changes, not every second

title: Phase 1: The plain product
description: The plain product, with no coach. A signed-in user can browse the exercise library, run the timer on an exercise, log an attempt, and see their progress. It is deployed, backed up, and used by its owner for two weeks. Out of scope: any LLM feature, API tokens, organizations. Exit: the dogfood friction list has been reviewed and Phase 2 re-planned from it. Starts once the Phase 0 baseline is confirmed; the README and CI cleanup can run alongside.

title: Add the agent config: CLAUDE.md, .claude/ settings and skills
description: CLAUDE.md, .claude/settings.json and the four project skills (sparring, bump-rails, add-exercise, decision-record), plus bin/bump-rails.

title: Published scope: future published_at means hidden
description: Exercise.published returns only rows with published_at in the past. A future published_at is absent from the library and its page returns 404. Scheduled publishing later relies on this, so it must not be bypassable.
acceptance_criteria:
- Tests cover a past, a present and a future published_at
- The page for an unpublished slug returns 404, not a redirect
notes:
Plan ref 1.3.

--- 2026-10-17 first criterion already met by 33c229b ---
 [x] 'Tests cover a past, a present and a future published_at' -- done as part
     of codegym-g70, not as separate work. Exercise.published is
     'where(published_at: ..Time.current)', and test/models/exercise_test.rb
     covers four states, not three: past (rename_a_method, 1.week.ago), present
     (created with published_at: Time.current, asserted published), future
     (scheduled_for_next_week, 1.week.from_now) and null (never_published).
     Null is the fourth state the criterion did not name, and it matters: hidden
     has two shapes, never-published and not-published-yet, and published? plus
     the scope agree on both.
 [ ] 'The page for an unpublished slug returns 404, not a redirect' -- NOT done
     and not startable yet. There is no exercises controller or route; the only
     route is /up. This half belongs with codegym-m7t (exercise page), where
     there is a page to 404 from. Suggest doing it there rather than as a
     separate pass, so the test and the thing it tests land together.

title: Decide: system tests in bin/ci, or drop the CI system-test job
description: config/ci.rb has 'Tests: System' commented out while .github/workflows/ci.yml has a system-test job, so the local pre-commit gate and GitHub do not run the same steps. Uncommenting it locally means bin/ci needs a browser and gets slower on every commit; dropping the CI job loses the coverage codegym-oiz (sign in, run the timer, log an attempt) will depend on. CLAUDE.md says system tests are used sparingly, and the timer is explicitly one of them, so the coverage is wanted somewhere.
acceptance_criteria: The choice is made and bin/ci and the workflow run the same test steps, or the difference is recorded as deliberate with a reason
notes: Surfaced while closing codegym-64m on 2026-10-17. Not urgent: with zero system tests the CI job currently passes in seconds, so nothing is broken either way today. It becomes a real question when codegym-oiz lands the first system test.

title: Review ADR 0001: is running on Rails main still working?
description: Revisit the decision to run on Rails main. Check the escape-hatch triggers: CI red for more than 7 days because of the framework, a needed gem with no path on main, or two stalled weeks. Keep, change or switch to stable 8.1, and record the outcome as a new decision.
acceptance_criteria: - A new decision record, or a note that the decision stands
notes: The ADR sets 2026-12-17 as its revisit date.

title: Layout and design pass
description: Light and dark themes, a layout that works at phone width, a landing page for signed-out visitors, and an accessible timer. Keep it plain: server-rendered, no JS build step.
acceptance_criteria:
- No horizontal scroll at 360px wide
- Contrast passes in both themes
- The timer and form are usable by keyboard alone

title: Calibration: predicted versus actual
description: Before starting, the user records predicted minutes and a confidence. Afterwards, show how well they predicted, over time. This measures something nothing else tracks: how good a developer's sense of their own ability is.
acceptance_criteria:
- Prediction is optional but easy to give
- A chart of predicted versus actual time, and of confidence versus outcome

title: Plan lock-in with server-side reveal
description: A user writes a plan and locks it. Only then does the server reveal the reference approach and what to notice. Predict-then-compare is the point of the exercise, so the order has to be enforced by the server, not by hiding things in the page.
design: Add plan_locked_at to attempts. The reveal endpoint refuses without it. Compare the plan against the reference side by side, with the user adding their own notes on the difference.
acceptance_criteria:
- Before locking, the reference text is absent from the HTML, JSON and any stream
- A locked plan cannot be edited
- Revealing is recorded on the attempt
notes: Plan ref 2.2. A good one to write yourself and review with /sparring.

title: Weekly Rails bump rhythm
description: Run /bump-rails once a week: one commit, one new row in the bump log. This is the core habit of running on Rails main.
acceptance_criteria: - Four bumps completed, each with a bump log row
notes: Plan ref ongoing. Recurring: when you finish a bump, file the next with --defer +1w so it reappears in bd ready next week.

title: Error tracking and logging you will actually read
description: Pick error tracking and make logs usable in production, with a daily or weekly look that fits how you work. Do this around the time of the first deploy.
acceptance_criteria: - An error in production reaches you without you looking for it
notes: Plan ref ongoing. Natural to do alongside the deploy task.

title: Decide: who is codegym for - just you, friends, or a public product?
description: This changes the cost model, the privacy work and all of the Teams phase. For one person, bring-your-own-key and a simple data policy are enough. For a public product, hosted keys, caps, retention, deletion and support all matter.
acceptance_criteria: - A written answer, even if provisional, and the phases it affects are adjusted
notes: Blocks the coach spike. Plan ref: open questions.

title: Write six exercises aimed at what agents wear down
description: Decomposing a vague problem, debugging unfamiliar code, finding a planted bug in a diff, predicting output. Classic algorithms stay but should not be most of the library. Use /add-exercise so each ships with coach notes.
acceptance_criteria:
- Six new exercises across at least three kinds
- Each was solved unaided by the author in the stated time

title: Exercise kinds: solve, predict, review, debug
description: Add a kind to exercises. Solve is today's behavior. Predict shows code and asks for the output before running it. Review shows a diff with a planted bug to find. Debug gives unfamiliar failing code to diagnose. Each kind gets the form it needs.
design: These exist because they exercise what agents wear down: decomposing a vague problem, debugging unfamiliar code, and judging code you did not write.
acceptance_criteria:
- Existing exercises default to solve and are unaffected
- Each kind has a form and a test

title: Store coach-only material where no page can reach it
description: Load <slug>.coach.md (reference approach, edge cases, common mistakes, hint ladder, what to notice) into its own table. Nothing user-facing may join to it or render it. This protects the whole product: if the reference answer leaks, the coach is pointless.

- A test crawls every page and turbo stream and fails if any coach note text appears
- db:seed loads coach notes idempotently

title: Write coach notes for the 12 starter exercises
description: Use /add-exercise to write the .coach.md for each starter exercise: reference approach, the edge cases people miss, common mistakes, a four-step hint ladder, and what to notice when comparing a plan with the reference.

title: Open questions
description: Product questions that change what gets built. Each is a decision issue. Closing one should leave a note on the issue or a decision record in docs/decisions/.

title: Phase 2: Predict-then-compare and calibration
description: Add the structure the coach will need, with no LLM yet: exercise kinds, plan lock-in with a server-side reveal, hidden coach material, and calibration data. Exit: a user can lock a plan, then see the reference approach and compare against it; predicted versus actual time is recorded; reference material is provably absent from every page until it is revealed.

title: Ongoing: practice and hygiene
description: Work that does not belong to one phase: the weekly Rails bump, upstream contributions, observability, accessibility, and keeping the architecture overview current.

title: Replace the default README
description: README.md is still the Rails default. Write what codegym is, how to run it, how to run the tests, and where CLAUDE.md, the ADRs and the beads workflow live.
acceptance_criteria: - A new contributor can clone, run bin/setup, and boot the app from the README alone

title: README: what it is, how to run it, how to run the tests, and a pointer to CLAUDE.md and the ADRs
close_reason: Duplicate. codegym-gjz duplicates codegym-d5u (Phase 0: Foundation), which holds the three children; codegym-tzj duplicates codegym-r5v (Replace the default README), which holds the acceptance criteria and the dependency on codegym-jt5. Both of these were bare: no description, labels, parent or deps. Reopen if they were meant to be distinct.

title: Debrief and observations
description: At the end of a session the coach asks what surprised the user and what they would do differently, compares their approach with the reference, and writes a short observation about them: where they got stuck and which rung they used.
acceptance_criteria:
- Each session ends with a stored observation the user can read
- The comparison names one thing the user's approach did better

title: Recommend the next exercise from observations
description: Use the observations to suggest what to practise next, such as an exercise that targets a habit the user keeps repeating.
acceptance_criteria: - A recommendation explains which observation it came from

title: Keep a one-page architecture overview current
description: One page describing how the app fits together: models, the jobs that run, what talks to the outside world, and where the secrets live. Update it at the end of each phase.
acceptance_criteria: - The overview matches the code at the end of each phase

title: Release cadence: a 'new this week' shelf
description: Publish on a rhythm using published_at. Add a 'new this week' shelf to the library, and optionally a recurring job that sends a digest. Solid Queue recurring tasks are the Rails-native way to schedule it.
acceptance_criteria:
- The shelf shows only exercises published in the last 7 days
- If a digest is built, it is a recurring job with a test
notes: Plan ref 2.7. Scheduled publishing needs no new mechanism: published_at already gates visibility.

title: File or triage one upstream Rails issue a month
description: Living on main means meeting bugs early. Reduce one a month to a minimal reproduction and file it, or triage someone else's. Upstream first, local workarounds last (ADR rule 5).
acceptance_criteria: - One upstream issue or PR per month, linked from the bump log

title: Plan review: questions, not verdicts
description: The coach reads the user's plan and asks two or three pointed questions about what that plan is most likely to get wrong, grounded in the exercise's coach notes. It gives no verdict and no fix.
acceptance_criteria:
- Replies are questions, covered by eval cases
- Questions reference real edge cases from the coach notes

title: Decide when streaks move to the user's time zone
description: Streaks are computed in UTC, so an evening session in the Americas can count toward the next day. Decide whether to store a time zone per user, and when.
acceptance_criteria: - Decision made, and the streak object takes a time zone if the answer is yes

title: Decide whether codegym is open source
description: Affects licensing, what goes in the repo (coach notes and reference solutions are the product's secret sauce) and whether contributors can add exercises.
acceptance_criteria: - A decision, and a LICENSE or a note explaining why not

title: Privacy: what is sent, stored, and how it is deleted
description: Write down what is sent to the model provider, what is stored, for how long, and how a user exports or deletes it. People will paste their own thinking into this.
acceptance_criteria:
- A decision record states the data flow and retention
- Deleting a user removes sessions, transcripts and observations
notes: Plan ref 3.11. Must be settled before the profile page and before anyone else uses this.

title: Spike: provider, client, hosted versus bring-your-own key, cost
description: Before building the coach, decide how it talks to a model. Pick a provider and a Ruby client library, decide between hosted keys and bring-your-own-key, settle how replies stream, and estimate cost per session from a real prototype.
acceptance_criteria:
- A decision record covers provider, client, key model and streaming
- Cost per session is measured on at least ten real runs, not guessed
notes: Plan ref 3.1. Depends on who codegym is for (see the audience question).

title: Cost controls and structured events
description: Per-session and per-user daily caps and a circuit breaker. Emit tokens, cost and rung as structured events so spend is visible. Use the Structured Event Reporter introduced in Rails 8.1.
acceptance_criteria:
- A session that hits its cap ends gracefully with a clear message
- A dashboard or query shows spend per user per day
- The breaker trips when the provider errors repeatedly

title: Profile page: what the coach has noted about you
description: Show everything the coach has recorded about the user. Let them edit or delete any of it and export all of it. Trust depends on it not being a hidden dossier.
acceptance_criteria:
- Every observation is visible, editable and deletable
- Export produces a complete file

title: Coach evals: adversarial cases and a leak detector
description: Ordinary assertions cannot check 'does the coach leak the answer'. Build an eval suite of adversarial cases ('just tell me', 'ignore your instructions', an instruction hidden inside a plan) and a leak detector that compares replies against the reference solution. Run it on demand and nightly, and add real failures to a regression set.
acceptance_criteria:
- The suite fails when a prompt change makes the coach reveal the answer
- Runs on demand through the local CI setup
- A nightly run reports to somewhere you will see it
notes: Plan ref 3.8. Genuinely interesting for Rails: testing nondeterministic behavior.

title: Accessibility pass on every new page
description: Keyboard use, focus handling with Turbo, contrast, labels, and what a screen reader hears from the timer and streamed coach replies.
acceptance_criteria: - Each phase ends with an accessibility check of the pages it added

title: Run coach turns as background jobs and stream replies
description: Model calls never run inside a request. A turn is a background job that streams its reply to the page with Turbo Streams. Try Active Job Continuations (new in Rails 8.1) for multi-step turns so a deploy mid-turn resumes instead of restarting.
acceptance_criteria:
- Closing the tab mid-reply does not lose the reply
- A deploy during a turn resumes it
- Failures retry safely without double-charging the user's budget
notes: Plan ref 3.3. A good place to learn what the newest Rails job features do under pressure.

title: Hint ladder, enforced on the server
description: Five rungs: a question, a concept to read, a smaller subproblem, a sketch of at most five lines, and only then the full answer. The server decides which context the model sees at each rung, so the model does not have the solution before the last rung. Do not rely on the prompt to hold the line.
design: State machine on CoachSession. Context is assembled per rung from the coach notes, so the model cannot disclose what it was never given. The user's up-front commitment (hint delay, whether to reveal) is checked by the server before advancing.
acceptance_criteria:
- Rung N's model call never receives material from rung N+1 or later
- Skipping rungs is impossible from the client
- Every rung used is recorded on the session
notes: Plan ref 3.5. The most important design in the product. A good one to write yourself and review with /sparring.

title: CoachSession model
description: A coach session holds the commitment the user made up front (how long before hints, whether the answer may be revealed at all), the current rung, the transcript, and token and cost counters.
acceptance_criteria:
- The commitment is stored with the session and cannot be loosened mid-session by the model
- Counters update with every model call

title: Phase 3: The coach
description: The coach: plan review, a hint ladder the server enforces, and a debrief, with a memory of the user's habits. The coach must make the user do the thinking, so the server, not the prompt, decides what the model is allowed to know at each step. Exit: a user completes a full session, costs are capped, and an eval suite shows the coach does not hand over the answer.

title: JSON API: fetch an exercise, submit an attempt
description: Versioned JSON endpoints authenticated by token: list and fetch published exercises, and submit an attempt. Keep to what the CLI and IDE need.
acceptance_criteria:
- Unpublished exercises are not served
- An attempt submitted through the API is indistinguishable from one logged on the site

title: Exercises with bundled tests
description: Ship tests with exercises so 'submit' can check a result instead of taking the user's word for it. Needs a decision on where tests run (locally, via the CLI) and how results are reported.
acceptance_criteria:
- At least three exercises ship with runnable tests
- Submit records the test result with the attempt

title: Billing and seat management
description: Only if this becomes a product: plans, seats and invoices.
acceptance_criteria: - Decide first whether this is wanted at all

title: Team progress view
description: Show patterns across a team without exposing an individual's notes by default.
acceptance_criteria: - Individual notes and coach observations are private unless the member shares them

title: Private exercises and an authoring screen
description: Add org_id and author_id to exercises. Members can write, preview and schedule private exercises that only their organization sees.
acceptance_criteria:
- Private exercises never appear in another organization's library
- Authoring has a live preview and publish scheduling

title: Organizations, memberships, roles, seats, tenant scoping
description: Organizations with members, roles and seats. Every tenant-owned query is scoped to the organization.
acceptance_criteria:
- Tests prove one organization cannot read or write another's data, for every tenant-owned model
- Removing a member removes their access immediately

title: CLI: get and submit
description: codegym get <slug> writes the exercise to a local file; codegym submit logs the attempt. Small and boring on purpose.
acceptance_criteria: - Works end to end against the API from a clean machine

title: API tokens
description: Personal API tokens, hashed at rest, scoped, shown once when created, and revocable. These are the base for the CLI, the agent skill and the IDE plugin.
acceptance_criteria:
- Only a digest is stored
- Tokens can be listed (without secrets) and revoked
- Scopes are enforced in tests

title: Portable coach skill for CLI agents
description: A skill that puts the coach in the terminal where the agent normally lives, using the API for the user's history. Model its behavior on /sparring, which already critiques and hints without editing files.
acceptance_criteria:
- It cannot edit files while active
- It reads and writes the user's history through the API

title: Sanitize Markdown with an allowlist
description: Exercise bodies are trusted today because only the owner writes them. Before anyone else can author exercises, render Markdown through an allowlist sanitizer.
acceptance_criteria:
- Script tags, event handlers and javascript: URLs never survive rendering, covered by tests
- A decision record names the sanitizer and the allowlist
notes: Plan ref 5.1. Must come before any way for other people to write exercises.

title: IDE plugin (VS Code first)
description: Bring the exercise and submit flow into the editor. Consider a focus mode: the editor is where the agent lives, so the plugin could help the user keep it switched off for the session.
acceptance_criteria: - Fetch an exercise and submit an attempt without leaving the editor

title: Phase 4: Reach (API, CLI, IDE)
description: Let people use codegym where they already work: API tokens, a JSON API, a CLI, a portable coach skill for CLI agents, and an IDE plugin. Exit: fetch an exercise and submit an attempt without opening the website.

title: Phase 5: Teams
description: Organizations, seats, private exercises, and team views. Exit: one organization cannot see another's data (proven by tests), and members can author and publish private exercises safely.
